svg.title: An HR role: who may edit the employee record — SoftTrack web design mockup (#246)
svg.desc: Start date, department and manager are set by the site admin, who is the IT role, and making HR a site admin hands over password resets and role grants. A separate flag lets an HR admin edit the employee record and keep the department list, and nothing else: no passwords, no deactivation, no roles, no money.
svg.text: An HR role: who may edit the employee record
· the record, kept by the people who know it
The record, in the hands of whoever keeps it

g.text: Settings → People operations → People, signed in as Grace
The employee record: what the organisation knows about each person. Passwords and access stay with the site admin.

svg.text: What the flag is, and is not

g.text: People operations is for HR admins
A site admin can grant HR access from Administration
→ Users. You followed a link to /settings/people.

svg.text: Done when is_hr_admin is a flag separate from site admin and finance admin, a site admin grants and revokes it with every change logged, an HR admin can set start date,
department, manager, title, location and employment type and see deactivated accounts, cannot reset passwords, deactivate accounts, grant roles or see money, and the routes sit
on an hr_router() with a sweep test.

g.text: somebody moved to Design is in
no role to grant. Those rows of
Routes sit on an hr_router() that puts the check in front of all of
them, with a sweep test over every HR route.
